evidenceCaveats: Exact Obsidian note reviewed in full; its market-validation verdict is a research claim, not observed adoption of these prototypes.
The note calls homeowner readiness validated but still asks whether homeowners trust agent commerce (lines 48–52, 125–132, 187–201). Test channel preference rather than assuming it.
AI adoption and click-to-call conversion do not establish willingness to order in chat (lines 23, 54–58).
Conversion figures are not return-rate measurements; design-build timeline statistics and the no-competitor claim do not establish Takeoff ROI (lines 21–25, 174).

painDefinitions.name: Duplicate-order prevention
painDefinitions.criterion: Existing PO lookup and duplicate check before release; visible order history alone is insufficient.

painDefinitions.name: Attributed approval routing
painDefinitions.criterion: Capture responsibility and cost before approval; preserve each role and decision.

painDefinitions.name: Delivery and receiving visibility
painDefinitions.criterion: Fresh supplier ETA, status provenance, receiving ownership; planning dates and access notes are not live tracking.

painDefinitions.name: Job and PO cost allocation
painDefinitions.criterion: Link receipts to job, PO, cost code and receiving record; a photo alone is insufficient.

painDefinitions.name: Quantity and specification return drivers
painDefinitions.criterion: Transparent quantities and waste, mismatch checks, return terms; no claim of reduced returns without a pilot.

painDefinitions.name: Complete, source-aware specifications
painDefinitions.criterion: Structured requirements, sources, preserved unknowns, supplier confirmation.

painDefinitions.name: Multi-party agreement
painDefinitions.criterion: Separate installation and budget decisions with attributed audit trail.

painDefinitions.name: Sample-to-order continuity
painDefinitions.criterion: Link sample request, identity, evidence and approval to the order; daylight inspection alone does not request a sample.
